title: Walla Walla Council
source:
{{Short description|1855 meeting between the United States and Native Americans}}

[[File:Walla Walla Council.jpg|thumb|The Walla Walla Council.]]
The '''Walla Walla Council (1855)''' was a meeting in the [[Pacific Northwest]] between the [[United States]] and sovereign [[Native Americans in the United States|tribal nations]] of the [[Cayuse people|Cayuse]], [[Nez Perce people|Nez Perce]], [[Umatilla people|Umatilla]], [[Walla Walla people|Walla Walla]], and [[Yakama]].<ref>{{cite journal
 | last = Trafzer
 | first = Clifford E.
 | date =Fall 2005
 | url = http://www.historycooperative.org/journals/ohq/106.3/trafzer.html
 | title = Legacy of the Walla Walla Council, 1855
 | journal = Oregon Historical Quarterly
 | volume = 106
 | issue = 3
 | pages = 398–411
 | doi = 10.1353/ohq.2005.0006
 | s2cid = 166019157
 | issn = 0030-4727
| url-access = subscription
 }}</ref> The council occurred on May 29 – June 11<!--, 1855-->;<ref>{{Cite web|title = Walla Walla 2020 {{!}} Walla Walla Treaty Council of 1855|url = http://ww2020.net/historic-sites/walla-walla-treaty-council-of-1855/|website = ww2020.net|accessdate = 14 December 2015}}</ref> the treaties signed at this council on June 9<ref>{{Cite web|title = Umatilla Relationships with US - Making Treaties|url = http://www.trailtribes.org/umatilla/making-treaties.htm|website = www.trailtribes.org|accessdate = 14 December 2015}}</ref> were ratified by the [[United States Senate|U.S. Senate]] four years later in [[36th United States Congress|1859]].<ref>{{cite book
  | last = United States Senate
  | authorlink = United States Senate
  | title = Journal of the Executive Proceedings of the Senate of the United States of America v.11
  |year= 1859
  | pages = 82
  | url = http://memory.loc.gov/ll/llej/011/0000/00840082.tif
}}
</ref>

These treaties codified the constitutional relationship between the people living on the [[Nez Perce]], [[Umatilla Indian Reservation|Umatilla]], and [[Yakama Indian Reservation|Yakama]] reservations; it was one of the earliest treaties obtained in the Pacific Northwest.

[[Washington Territory]]'s first [[List of governors of Washington|governor]] [[Isaac I. Stevens]] secured this treaty, allowing larger portions of the land to be given to the two largest and most powerful tribes: Yakama and Nez Perce; these reservations encompassed most of their traditional hunting grounds. The smaller tribes moved to the smaller of the three reservations. Stevens was able to acquire {{convert|45000|sqmi|spell=in}} of land.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Schwantes|first1=Carlos Arnaldo|title=The Pacific Northwest|date=1996|publisher=University of Nebraska Press|location=Lincoln|isbn=0-8032-4225-5}}</ref>

The United States government later [[List of United States treaties#U.S.–Native American treaties|violated these treaties]], first by failing to pay the agreed sum for the ceded land,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lapwai |first=Mailing Address: Nez Perce National Historical Park 39063 US Hwy 95 |last2=Us |first2=ID 83540-9715 Phone: 208 843-7001 Contact |title=Aftermath - Nez Perce National Historical Park (U.S. National Park Service) |url=https://www.nps.gov/nepe/learn/historyculture/aftermath-of-1855-treaty.htm |access-date=2024-06-15 |website=www.nps.gov |language=en}}</ref> and later by reducing the Nez Perce reservation by 90% and [[Nez Perce War|forcibly removing the Nez Perce]] from their lands affirmed by the 1855 treaty.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Treaty with the Nez Perces 1855 |url=https://critfc.org/member-tribes-overview/nez-perce-tribe/treaty-with-the-nez-perces-1855/ |access-date=2024-06-15 |website=CRITFC |language=en-US}}</ref>
